title: Further Reading Entry
description: One work on the /reading list of the State of AI in Design Systems study: writing, talks and courses about what happens when a design system meets an AI agent. Unlike the rest of the dataset, this list is not frozen at the July 2026 snapshot — its published date is computed from the newest `added_on` below. Every entry links to a page that was read before it was listed.

id.description: kebab-case slug, e.g. 'design-systems-need-evals'. A correction names a record by it, the way a data correction names 'systems/primer-github'.

title.description: The work's own title, as the page gives it.

author.description: Who made it. A publication rather than a person when the work carries no byline.

published.description: ISO date the work was published. Omitted only when the work genuinely has no publication date — a rolling course, or a page that is revised rather than dated.

kind.description: What sort of work it is. The list renders these groups in this order, so work reporting data and instruments you can run against your own system come before commentary about the field.

url.description: The page this entry was read from. Required, and held to the same bar as a record's source_url: a page that loads and shows the thing.

description.description: What the work says, on its own terms. Not what it means for this report — a neutral description ages well and needs no claim about this study's own coverage.

quote.description: A short verbatim line from the work, present when the work has one that does the arguing. Quoted exactly, from the page at `url`.

price.description: Present when the work costs money. A reading list that sends someone to a checkout without saying so is not serving them.

amount.description: As the page states it, currency included, e.g. '$995'.

buys.description: What that buys, e.g. '20+ hours across six chapters, plus a Slack community'.

added_on.description: ISO date this entry was added to the list. The newest of these is the list's published last-updated date, which is why it is computed rather than typed.
